newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Cowie eyes bus buys in Europe.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Cowie eyes bus buys in Europe.

text.p: Cowie Group Plc, the transport to retail combine, aims to increase its market share in the UK by two to three percent this year through acquisitions and is talking about possible deals in mainland Europe.

Gordon Hodgson, Cowie chief executive, told Reuters in the interview "It would be nice if we could get an extra two to three percent (on UK market share) this year. In Europe, we are also looking for a platform -- possibly in Scandanavia and the Netherlands, in particular," he said.

In the UK, Hodgson said the group wanted to strengthen its operation in Scotland were "we are not strong". He disagreed with the view of some other bus rivals, including Stagecoach Plc, that UK bus companies were too expensive at present.
"If it slots into your existing business and there are savings from economies of scale, then it is not expensive. So I don't agree with that view," he said.
Hodgson added Cowie would "keep mopping up" small operations to augment its presence at home as well as looking to plug gaps in Scotland.
Asked how much the group was willing to spend on acquisitions this year, the chief executive said "We could do a 50 million pounds deal easily,"
The other opportunity seen is quality partnerships with local authority groups in the UK, involving rebranding and revamping of services.
In such cases, increases in usage of the service could average at 7-8 percent, said Hodgson.

Asked whether Cowie would be interested in investing in the London Underground tube system which is currently under review with a view to getting the private sector involved, Hodgson said: "We would be interested in taking a segment of it."
This refers to one possible option of the government selling franchises for the individual metro lines to private sector operators.
Asked to comment on current trading, he remained circumspect saying the interim results were indicative of current conditions. "By and large" the group is on track for the full year, he said.
